title: Mixed contexts: a changed routine, a chosen practice, or an inference

constructions.label: a practice the person consciously maintains
a current judgment supported by evidence

relationships.label: what has changed / what someone makes a practice of / what the evidence suggests

exercises.prompt: 去年までは雑誌をほとんど読まなかった。電車で通勤を始め、待ち時間に開いているうちに、いつの間にか読書が日課になった。特に毎日の目標を決めているわけではない。今は通勤中、毎日雑誌を読む____。
exercises.translation: Choose an appropriate form of ようになる, ようにする, ことにする, はずだ or ようだ. Fill the whole ending in hiragana, using one complete, uncontracted plain-form construction; keep any copula and do not add particles or auxiliary constructions. Until last year I hardly read magazines. After starting to commute by train, reading during the wait gradually became a routine without my setting a daily goal. I have now come to read magazines every day on the commute. 日課 (にっか) means daily routine.
exercises.evidence: The speaker reports a known before-and-now change in behavior, not a present effort rule or a guess about the routine.
exercises.explanation: 読むようになった reports the change; 読むようになっている presents the resulting routine as the current state. Both endings fit. The printed 読む stays outside the blank. ようにしている would foreground deliberate care, and ことにしている a chosen practice, rather than this unplanned development. はずだ／ようだ would turn the direct report into an inference. Those constructions are not globally incompatible with reading; they express a different message from this translation. The same pool is used throughout this set, so it does not tell you which function applies.

options.label: ようになった
options.rationale: Reports the established change from rarely reading to a daily routine.

options.label: ようにしている
options.rationale: Would make deliberate maintenance the point, rather than the unplanned change described.

options.label: はずだ
options.rationale: Would infer the reading habit rather than directly report the speaker's changed behavior.

exercises.prompt: 会議で話についていけるよう、以前から準備の項目を決め、毎回チェックしている。うっかり読み忘れる日もあるので、今も意識して続けている。会議がある日の朝には、事前の資料を読む____。
exercises.translation: Choose an appropriate form of ようになる, ようにする, ことにする, はずだ or ようだ. Fill the whole ending in hiragana, using one complete, uncontracted plain-form construction; keep any copula and do not add particles or auxiliary constructions. To follow meetings, I have long kept a preparation checklist and still check it each time. I sometimes forget to read, so I continue to make a conscious effort. On meeting mornings, I make a practice of reading the advance materials. 資料 (しりょう) means materials or documents.
exercises.evidence: This is a long-standing, deliberately maintained preparation rule that can still have lapses, not a newly established routine.
exercises.explanation: 読むようにしている foregrounds the continuing care or effort; 読むことにしている presents the same preparation as a chosen standing practice. 読むようにする also fits as a generic account of repeated care on meeting mornings, not necessarily a new undertaking; ようにしている makes the maintained state more explicit. All three fit here. ようになった would report a change in behavior, not the ongoing maintenance described. はずだ／ようだ would make an inference rather than state this known self-imposed practice. Merely announcing a new decision with ことにする or retelling the original decision with ことにした would change the focus. Effort does not guarantee perfect performance.

options.label: ようになった
options.rationale: Would foreground a new change rather than the existing practice being consciously maintained.

options.label: ようにしている
options.rationale: Reports the ongoing effort; ことにしている also fits the personal-rule framing.

options.label: はずだ
options.rationale: Would infer what the speaker does rather than describe the maintained practice directly.

exercises.prompt: 同僚は自分で新聞を買っていると言っていた。机には毎朝その日の新聞があり、本文には書き込みもある。読んでいるところを直接見たわけではないが、この様子から判断すると、同僚は毎朝新聞を読む____。
exercises.translation: Choose an appropriate form of ようになる, ようにする, ことにする, はずだ or ようだ. Fill the whole ending in hiragana, using one complete, uncontracted plain-form construction; keep any copula and do not add particles or auxiliary constructions. My coworker said they buy newspapers, and each morning that day's paper is on the desk with notes in the text. I have not directly watched them read. Judging from these signs, they apparently read a newspaper every morning. 本文 (ほんぶん) means the main text.
exercises.evidence: The speaker draws a present conclusion from marked newspapers rather than observing a change or knowing the coworker's chosen policy.
exercises.explanation: 読むはずだ gives a reasoned expectation, while 読むようだ presents what the evidence suggests. Both fit this current judgment; はずである and ようである are also accepted plain predicates, with a more formal written tone. They are not claimed to have identical nuance or fixed confidence percentages. ようになった would assert a change without an earlier baseline, while ようにしている would assert deliberate maintenance that these traces alone do not establish. The evidence is informative, not proof of every day's behavior.

options.label: ようになった
options.rationale: Would assert a change in routine without evidence of what the earlier routine was.

options.label: ようにしている
options.rationale: Would assert a conscious practice rather than the supported judgment about behavior.

options.label: はずだ
options.rationale: Makes a present judgment from the available evidence; ようだ also fits.

exercises.prompt: 以前は日記をまったく書かなかった。三か月間、自分で決めて毎晩続けた結果、今では特に意識しなくても自然にノートを開く。以前と違い、今は毎晩日記を書く____。
exercises.translation: Choose an appropriate form of ようになる, ようにする, ことにする, はずだ or ようだ. Fill the whole ending in hiragana, using one complete, uncontracted plain-form construction; keep any copula and do not add particles or auxiliary constructions. I used not to keep a diary. After deliberately continuing every night for three months, I now open the notebook naturally, without special effort. Unlike before, I have now come to write a diary every evening.
exercises.evidence: Deliberate practice led to an actual change that is now established; the current statement reports that result.
exercises.explanation: 書くようになった reports the acquired routine, and 書くようになっている reports the resulting current state. Both are accepted. This change was deliberately cultivated: なる does not mean nobody acted intentionally. ようにしている／ことにしている could describe the earlier practice or another account of the process, but the current English report focuses on the established change rather than continued conscious maintenance. はずだ／ようだ would replace that direct result report with an inference.

options.label: ようになった
options.rationale: Reports the new routine that the earlier deliberate practice produced.

options.label: ことにしている
options.rationale: Would foreground the personal rule instead of the established change being reported now.

options.label: ようだ
options.rationale: Would make a tentative judgment rather than directly report the achieved change.

exercises.prompt: アイデアを忘れないために、思いついたら記録するという自分のルールを以前から続けている。まだ忘れることもあるので、毎回意識してペンを取る。何か思いついたときは、その場でノートに書く____。
exercises.translation: Choose an appropriate form of ようになる, ようにする, ことにする, はずだ or ようだ. Fill the whole ending in hiragana, using one complete, uncontracted plain-form construction; keep any copula and do not add particles or auxiliary constructions. I have long maintained my own rule of recording ideas so I do not forget them. I still sometimes forget, so each time I consciously reach for a pen. Whenever an idea occurs to me, I make a practice of writing it in my notebook there and then.
exercises.evidence: The speaker is describing an existing self-imposed rule and the effort to keep following it.
exercises.explanation: 書くことにしている presents the standing personal rule; 書くようにしている foregrounds the continuing care. 書くようにする also fits the recurring 'whenever an idea occurs' frame as a generic account of repeated care; ようにしている more explicitly presents it as a maintained practice. All three suit this account. ようになった would report a new behavioral change, while はずだ／ようだ would report what the evidence suggests, not the rule the speaker knows they are maintaining. The model does not claim flawless automatic behavior: the context expressly allows forgetting. The current report is not merely the original act of deciding to adopt the rule.

options.label: ようになった
options.rationale: Would foreground a newly established behavior rather than the rule being maintained.

options.label: ことにしている
options.rationale: States the standing personal rule; ようにしている also fits the continuing effort.

options.label: ようだ
options.rationale: Would infer the behavior instead of directly describing this known practice.

exercises.prompt: 友人が公開している日記には、この一か月、毎晩新しい記事が出ている。実際に書く場面や時刻を確認したわけではないが、この更新記録から判断すると、友人は毎日日記を書く____。
exercises.translation: Choose an appropriate form of ようになる, ようにする, ことにする, はずだ or ようだ. Fill the whole ending in hiragana, using one complete, uncontracted plain-form construction; keep any copula and do not add particles or auxiliary constructions. A new entry has appeared in my friend's public diary every evening this month. I have not checked the actual writing or its timing. Judging from the update record, my friend apparently writes a diary every day. 更新 (こうしん) means updating.
exercises.evidence: Regular updates support a judgment about regular writing, but the actual writing schedule has not been verified.
exercises.explanation: 書くようだ and 書くはずだ both express a present judgment supported by the record, with different shades of evidential impression and reasoned expectation. ようである／はずである are accepted formal plain alternatives. Publication times do not guarantee writing times: scheduled or prepared entries remain possible, which is why this is an inference rather than verified observation. ようになった would add an unsupported before-and-after change; ことにしている would assert a chosen rule that the update record does not reveal.

options.label: ようになった
options.rationale: Would assert a change without information about the friend's earlier writing habits.

options.label: ことにしている
options.rationale: Would assert a personal rule rather than infer the behavior from the record.

options.label: ようだ
options.rationale: States what the updates suggest; はずだ also fits a reasoned-expectation framing.

exercises.prompt: 職場の端末がすべて新しいソフトに切り替わり、以前のソフトはなくなった。私が自分の習慣として選んだわけではないが、毎日の作業で使うものは変わった。今は仕事で新しいソフトを使う____。
exercises.translation: Choose an appropriate form of ようになる, ようにする, ことにする, はずだ or ようだ. Fill the whole ending in hiragana, using one complete, uncontracted plain-form construction; keep any copula and do not add particles or auxiliary constructions. All the workplace terminals switched to new software, and the old software is gone. I did not choose this as a personal habit, but what I use in my daily work has changed. I now use the new software as the resulting routine. 端末 (たんまつ) means terminal.
exercises.evidence: A workplace change has produced an actual new pattern of use, not the speaker's chosen practice or a prediction.
exercises.explanation: 使うようになっている presents the changed routine as the current state; 使うようになった reports the transition. Both fit. This is a change in use, not a newly acquired skill, so the printed dictionary form 使う stays unchanged. ようにしている would foreground deliberate maintenance, and はずだ／ようだ would infer use rather than report it directly. An arrangement account with ことになった can be natural elsewhere, but ことになる is not in this set's common five-pattern pool; it is not declared globally wrong.

options.label: ようになっている
options.rationale: Reports the new software use as the current result of the workplace change.

options.label: ようにしている
options.rationale: Would foreground a chosen effort rather than the resulting usage pattern described.

options.label: はずだ
options.rationale: Would make a judgment about likely use instead of directly reporting the new routine.

exercises.prompt: 使い捨ての袋を減らすため、以前から買い物前に布の袋をかばんへ入れると決めている。持っていくのを忘れることもあるので、今も出発前に意識して確かめる。買い物では布の袋を使う____。
exercises.translation: Choose an appropriate form of ようになる, ようにする, ことにする, はずだ or ようだ. Fill the whole ending in hiragana, using one complete, uncontracted plain-form construction; keep any copula and do not add particles or auxiliary constructions. To reduce disposable bags, I have long had a rule of packing a cloth bag before shopping. I sometimes forget it, so I still consciously check before leaving. I make a practice of using a cloth bag for shopping. 使い捨て (つかいすて) means disposable.
exercises.evidence: The speaker maintains a chosen practice through deliberate preparation, with occasional lapses.
exercises.explanation: 使うようにしている emphasizes conscious care, while 使うことにしている emphasizes the standing rule. 使うようにする also fits as a generic account of care on recurring shopping trips, rather than necessarily announcing a new intention. All three fit; ようにしている more explicitly foregrounds the maintained state. ようになった would report the adoption or establishment of a new routine instead of the continuing practice described here. はずだ／ようだ would change the statement into an inference. The aim to reduce disposable bags does not assert that the cloth bag is used on absolutely every trip, and none of these practice expressions guarantees success.

options.label: ようになった
options.rationale: Would foreground a behavioral transition rather than ongoing deliberate maintenance.

options.label: ようにしている
options.rationale: Describes the ongoing care; ことにしている also fits the rule the speaker maintains.

options.label: はずだ
options.rationale: Would infer bag use rather than report the speaker's maintained practice directly.

exercises.prompt: 友人は買い物に出るとき布の袋を持ち、帰りにはその袋に品物が入っている。これを何度も見たが、本人の方針やすべての買い物を確認したわけではない。この様子から判断すると、友人は普段の買い物で布の袋を使う____。
exercises.translation: Choose an appropriate form of ようになる, ようにする, ことにする, はずだ or ようだ. Fill the whole ending in hiragana, using one complete, uncontracted plain-form construction; keep any copula and do not add particles or auxiliary constructions. I have repeatedly seen my friend leave for shopping with a cloth bag and return with goods in it. I have not checked their policy or every shopping trip. From these observations, they apparently use a cloth bag for their usual shopping. 方針 (ほうしん) means policy.
exercises.evidence: Repeated observations support a general judgment about habitual use, without establishing a new change or the person's intention.
exercises.explanation: 使うはずだ and 使うようだ fit the current inference from repeated observations; はずである and ようである are accepted formal plain forms. Seeing some instances supports a habitual-use judgment but does not independently prove every trip or reveal the person's private rule. ようになった would add a change from an earlier routine; ようにしている would present deliberate care rather than the behavior inferred here. Do not assign numerical confidence levels to the accepted inferential alternatives.

options.label: ようになった
options.rationale: Would assert a new transition without evidence about earlier bag use.

options.label: ようにしている
options.rationale: Would assert conscious maintenance instead of the evidence-based judgment requested.

options.label: はずだ
options.rationale: Draws a current conclusion from the observations; ようだ also fits.

exercises.prompt: 英語は以前から話せたが、職場の会議は日本語だった。海外の同僚が加わって会議の共通語が英語になり、実際に話す言葉も変わった。今は毎週の会議で英語で話す____。
exercises.translation: Choose an appropriate form of ようになる, ようにする, ことにする, はずだ or ようだ. Fill the whole ending in hiragana, using one complete, uncontracted plain-form construction; keep any copula and do not add particles or auxiliary constructions. I could already speak English, but our workplace meetings used to be in Japanese. After colleagues overseas joined, English became the common meeting language, and my actual language use changed too. I have now come to speak English in the weekly meetings.
exercises.evidence: The language ability existed before; the established change is in the language actually used in meetings.
exercises.explanation: 話すようになった reports the changed behavior; 話すようになっている reports its current result. Both fit the translation. The printed 話す describes actual use, not a new ability, so do not change it to 話せる inside the answer. ようにしている／ことにしている would foreground a chosen practice instead of this before-and-after report. はずだ／ようだ would turn it into an inference. The change can arise from deliberate decisions about a workplace without なる itself meaning 'unintentional'.

options.label: ようになった
options.rationale: Reports the established change in the language used, not a new speaking ability.

options.label: ことにしている
options.rationale: Would foreground a personal practice rather than report the actual change in meeting language.

options.label: ようだ
options.rationale: Would infer the language use instead of directly reporting the changed routine.

exercises.prompt: 答えを分かりやすくするため、以前から自分の説明の順序を決めている。細かい話から始めてしまうこともあるので、今も答える前に意識して確認する。質問に答えるときは、まず結論から話す____。
exercises.translation: Choose an appropriate form of ようになる, ようにする, ことにする, はずだ or ようだ. Fill the whole ending in hiragana, using one complete, uncontracted plain-form construction; keep any copula and do not add particles or auxiliary constructions. I have long had my own rule for ordering explanations so answers are clear. I sometimes start with details, so I still consciously check before answering. When answering questions, I make a practice of stating the conclusion first. 結論 (けつろん) means conclusion.
exercises.evidence: The speaker describes a standing explanation policy and the ongoing effort to follow it, including occasional lapses.
exercises.explanation: 話すことにしている states the chosen rule; 話すようにしている emphasizes the care taken to follow it. 話すようにする also fits the recurring 'when answering questions' frame as a generic account of repeated care; ようにしている more explicitly foregrounds the maintained practice. All three fit. ようになった would report a change rather than the current maintenance of this older rule. はずだ／ようだ would infer the behavior rather than directly report the known practice. Beginning with details sometimes does not negate the intention to follow the practice; none of the accepted expressions promises error-free execution.

options.label: ようになった
options.rationale: Would foreground an acquired routine rather than the existing policy being maintained.

options.label: ことにしている
options.rationale: Describes the standing policy; ようにしている also fits the continuing care.

options.label: ようだ
options.rationale: Would make an inference instead of stating the speaker's own maintained practice.

exercises.prompt: その講師の四つの講演録音を聞くと、どれも質問への答えは結論から始まっている。本人の方針やほかの場面は知らないが、録音から判断すると、その講師は質問に答えるとき、まず結論から話す____。
exercises.translation: Choose an appropriate form of ようになる, ようにする, ことにする, はずだ or ようだ. Fill the whole ending in hiragana, using one complete, uncontracted plain-form construction; keep any copula and do not add particles or auxiliary constructions. In four recordings of this lecturer, the answers to questions all begin with the conclusion. I do not know the lecturer's policy or their behavior in other settings. Judging from the recordings, they apparently state the conclusion first when answering questions. 講演 (こうえん) means lecture.
exercises.evidence: The recordings support a current judgment about a recurring behavior, not a claim about its origin or conscious intention.
exercises.explanation: 話すようだ presents what the recordings suggest; 話すはずだ can frame it as a reasoned expectation. ようである／はずである are accepted formal plain variants. This shared class does not require the two formulations to convey identical certainty. ようになった would assert a change with no earlier comparison, while ことにしている would attribute a chosen rule not established by the recordings. Other inference markers can be natural in wider Japanese, but the common five-pattern pool defines this exercise.

options.label: ようになった
options.rationale: Would assert a transition without evidence of the lecturer's earlier style.

options.label: ことにしている
options.rationale: Would assert a personal rule rather than judge the recurring behavior from the sample.

options.label: ようだ
options.rationale: States the inference from the recordings; はずだ also fits a reasoned-expectation framing.
